body: # AADL Scope Notes

This Ksyn note summarizes AADL scope knowledge used by AGREE-AutoGen during architecture grounding and fusion. The AADL AS5506C standard is recorded through `raw/ksyn/AADL_AS5506C.local_source.md`; the raw standard PDF is not redistributed in this repository.
## Architecture Grounding

The authoritative source for component names, ports, directions, data types, subcomponents, and connections is the input AADL model. The Model Analyst Agent extracts this structure before AGREE generation and fusion.
## Component Type and Implementation Scope

AGREE assumptions and guarantees that refer to component ports should be placed in valid component type scopes. Implementation-level bindings should be placed in implementation scopes after relevant subcomponents and connections. Subcomponent ports should not be used in a component type contract unless represented through valid variables or outputs.
## Package and Feature References

AADL package references require matching `with` clauses. Generated AGREE code should not introduce package-qualified identifiers, data types, or property references that are absent from the analyzed model and its configured dependencies.
# AGREE Syntax Notes

This Ksyn note summarizes AGREE syntax and semantic knowledge used by AGREE-AutoGen. It is aligned with `raw/ksyn/AGREE_knowledge_dataset_en.pdf`, `raw/ksyn/AGREE_Users_Guide.pdf`, the Kdef rules, and the code examples in Kexp.
## Annex and Clause Structure

AGREE contracts are written inside `annex agree {** ... **};` blocks. Component type annexes are the normal location for assumptions, guarantees, constants, and equation declarations. Component implementation annexes are used for implementation-level bindings such as assignments when they are valid in that scope.
Common clause forms include:
- `assume "label": expression;` - `guarantee "label": expression;` - `eq name : type = expression;` - `const name : type = value;` - `assign output = expression;`
## Temporal and Expression Patterns

Stateful equations should use initialized temporal recurrence, for example `0.0 -> pre(t) + step`. Branching logic should use nested `if ... then ... else`. Generated contracts should use AGREE logical operators such as `and`, `or`, `not(...)`, and implication `=>`.
## Type and Reference Constraints

Generated expressions should preserve type consistency. Numeric variables should receive numeric expressions, Boolean variables should receive Boolean expressions, and package-qualified references should match imports and available model units. Helper functions should only be used when defined by the model or imported package.
# AADL AS5506C Local Source
AADL AS5506C is used as a Ksyn source for AADL architecture, component, feature, port, implementation, and annex-scope knowledge.

The raw standard PDF is not redistributed in this repository. The release records the source boundary here and includes the derived scope notes used by AGREE-AutoGen in `knowledge_base/processed/ksyn/aadl_scope_notes.md`.

package agree_kexp_range_monitor public with Base_Types; data real extends Base_Types::Float end real; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system RangeMonitorExample features value_in : in data port real; safe_flag : out data port bool; annex agree {** const lower_limit : real = 0.0; const upper_limit : real = 100.0; eq value_in_range : bool = value_in >= lower_limit and value_in <= upper_limit; assume "input value is finite within broad engineering bounds": value_in > -1000000.0 and value_in < 1000000.0; guarantee "safe flag follows the declared numeric range": safe_flag = value_in_range; **}; end RangeMonitorExample; system implementation RangeMonitorExample.impl end RangeMonitorExample.impl; end agree_kexp_range_monitor;

package agree_kexp_recurrence public with Base_Types; data real extends Base_Types::Float end real; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system RecurrenceExample features enable_step : in data port bool; state_out : out data port real; annex agree {** const step_size : real = 0.5; eq state_value : real = 0.0 -> if enable_step then pre(state_value) + step_size else pre(state_value); guarantee "state output follows the recurrent state": state_out = state_value; **}; end RecurrenceExample; system implementation RecurrenceExample.impl end RecurrenceExample.impl; end agree_kexp_recurrence;

package agree_kexp_conditional_selection public with Base_Types; data int extends Base_Types::Integer end int; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system ConditionalSelectionExample features select_first : in data port bool; input_a : in data port int; input_b : in data port int; selected_value : out data port int; annex agree {** eq chosen_value : int = if select_first then input_a else input_b; guarantee "selected output follows the selector": selected_value = chosen_value; **}; end ConditionalSelectionExample; system implementation ConditionalSelectionExample.impl end ConditionalSelectionExample.impl; end agree_kexp_conditional_selection;

package agree_kexp_boolean_logic public with Base_Types; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system BooleanLogicExample features condition_a : in data port bool; condition_b : in data port bool; condition_c : in data port bool; decision : out data port bool; annex agree {** eq two_conditions_hold : bool = (condition_a and condition_b) or (condition_a and condition_c) or (condition_b and condition_c); guarantee "decision requires at least two active conditions": decision = two_conditions_hold; **}; end BooleanLogicExample; system implementation BooleanLogicExample.impl end BooleanLogicExample.impl; end agree_kexp_boolean_logic;

package agree_kexp_output_envelope public with Base_Types; data real extends Base_Types::Float end real; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system OutputEnvelopeExample features raw_input : in data port real; bounded_output : out data port real; was_limited : out data port bool; annex agree {** const min_output : real = -1.0; const max_output : real = 1.0; eq clamped_output : real = if raw_input < min_output then min_output else if raw_input > max_output then max_output else raw_input; eq limit_applied : bool = raw_input < min_output or raw_input > max_output; guarantee "bounded output remains within the envelope": bounded_output >= min_output and bounded_output <= max_output; guarantee "bounded output equals the clamped value": bounded_output = clamped_output; guarantee "limit flag records whether clamping was required": was_limited = limit_applied; **}; end OutputEnvelopeExample; system implementation OutputEnvelopeExample.impl end OutputEnvelopeExample.impl; end agree_kexp_output_envelope;

package agree_kexp_integrated_pattern public with Base_Types; data int extends Base_Types::Integer end int; data real extends Base_Types::Float end real; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system RangeMonitorExample features value_in : in data port real; safe_flag : out data port bool; annex agree {** const lower_limit : real = 0.0; const upper_limit : real = 100.0; eq value_in_range : bool = value_in >= lower_limit and value_in <= upper_limit; guarantee "safe flag follows the declared numeric range": safe_flag = value_in_range; **}; end RangeMonitorExample; system implementation RangeMonitorExample.impl end RangeMonitorExample.impl; system ConditionalSelectionExample features select_first : in data port bool; input_a : in data port int; input_b : in data port int; selected_value : out data port int; annex agree {** eq chosen_value : int = if select_first then input_a else input_b; guarantee "selected output follows the selector": selected_value = chosen_value; **}; end ConditionalSelectionExample; system implementation ConditionalSelectionExample.impl end ConditionalSelectionExample.impl; system IntegratedPatternExample features source_value : in data port real; selector : in data port bool; input_left : in data port int; input_right : in data port int; final_safe_flag : out data port bool; final_selected_value : out data port int; end IntegratedPatternExample; system implementation IntegratedPatternExample.impl subcomponents monitor : system RangeMonitorExample.impl; chooser : system ConditionalSelectionExample.impl; connections c1 : port source_value -> monitor.value_in; c2 : port monitor.safe_flag -> final_safe_flag; c3 : port selector -> chooser.select_first; c4 : port input_left -> chooser.input_a; c5 : port input_right -> chooser.input_b; c6 : port chooser.selected_value -> final_selected_value; end IntegratedPatternExample.impl; end agree_kexp_integrated_pattern;

package agree_kexp_counter_threshold public with Base_Types; data int extends Base_Types::Integer end int; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system CounterThresholdExample features reset_counter : in data port bool; increment_counter : in data port bool; threshold_reached : out data port bool; annex agree {** const threshold_value : int = 4; eq counter : int = 0 -> if reset_counter then 0 else if increment_counter then pre(counter) + 1 else pre(counter); guarantee "threshold flag follows counter threshold": threshold_reached = (counter >= threshold_value); **}; end CounterThresholdExample; system implementation CounterThresholdExample.impl end CounterThresholdExample.impl; end agree_kexp_counter_threshold;

package agree_kexp_mode_transition public with Base_Types; data int extends Base_Types::Integer end int; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system ModeTransitionExample features reset_mode : in data port bool; advance_mode : in data port bool; mode_out : out data port int; annex agree {** const mode_zero : int = 0; const mode_one : int = 1; const mode_two : int = 2; eq mode : int = mode_zero -> if reset_mode then mode_zero else if advance_mode and pre(mode) = mode_zero then mode_one else if advance_mode and pre(mode) = mode_one then mode_two else pre(mode); guarantee "mode output mirrors internal mode": mode_out = mode; guarantee "mode remains in the declared range": mode >= mode_zero and mode <= mode_two; **}; end ModeTransitionExample; system implementation ModeTransitionExample.impl end ModeTransitionExample.impl; end agree_kexp_mode_transition;

package agree_kexp_input_validity public with Base_Types; data real extends Base_Types::Float end real; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system InputValidityExample features numeric_input : in data port real; boolean_input : in data port bool; valid_output : out data port bool; annex agree {** const valid_min : real = -50.0; const valid_max : real = 50.0; eq numeric_valid : bool = numeric_input >= valid_min and numeric_input <= valid_max; eq boolean_valid : bool = boolean_input = true or boolean_input = false; guarantee "valid output is true only for valid numeric and boolean inputs": valid_output = (numeric_valid and boolean_valid); **}; end InputValidityExample; system implementation InputValidityExample.impl end InputValidityExample.impl; end agree_kexp_input_validity;

package agree_kexp_pairwise_consistency public with Base_Types; data int extends Base_Types::Integer end int; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system PairwiseConsistencyExample features primary_value : in data port int; secondary_value : in data port int; difference_ok : out data port bool; annex agree {** const max_difference : int = 10; eq difference_nonnegative : int = if primary_value >= secondary_value then primary_value - secondary_value else secondary_value - primary_value; guarantee "difference flag follows the allowed difference": difference_ok = (difference_nonnegative <= max_difference); **}; end PairwiseConsistencyExample; system implementation PairwiseConsistencyExample.impl end PairwiseConsistencyExample.impl; end agree_kexp_pairwise_consistency;

package agree_kexp_history_comparison public with Base_Types; data real extends Base_Types::Float end real; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system HistoryComparisonExample features observed_value : in data port real; nondecreasing : out data port bool; annex agree {** eq initialized : bool = false -> true; guarantee "history comparison is skipped at initialization": not initialized => nondecreasing; guarantee "after initialization observed value is nondecreasing": initialized => nondecreasing = (observed_value >= pre(observed_value)); **}; end HistoryComparisonExample; system implementation HistoryComparisonExample.impl end HistoryComparisonExample.impl; end agree_kexp_history_comparison;

package agree_kexp_combined_pattern public with Base_Types; data int extends Base_Types::Integer end int; data bool extends Base_Types::Boolean end bool; system CounterThresholdExample features reset_counter : in data port bool; increment_counter : in data port bool; threshold_reached : out data port bool; annex agree {** const threshold_value : int = 4; eq counter : int = 0 -> if reset_counter then 0 else if increment_counter then pre(counter) + 1 else pre(counter); guarantee "threshold flag follows counter threshold": threshold_reached = (counter >= threshold_value); **}; end CounterThresholdExample; system implementation CounterThresholdExample.impl end CounterThresholdExample.impl; system PairwiseConsistencyExample features primary_value : in data port int; secondary_value : in data port int; difference_ok : out data port bool; annex agree {** const max_difference : int = 10; eq difference_nonnegative : int = if primary_value >= secondary_value then primary_value - secondary_value else secondary_value - primary_value; guarantee "difference flag follows the allowed difference": difference_ok = (difference_nonnegative <= max_difference); **}; end PairwiseConsistencyExample; system implementation PairwiseConsistencyExample.impl end PairwiseConsistencyExample.impl; system CombinedPatternExample features reset : in data port bool; step : in data port bool; value_a : in data port int; value_b : in data port int; status : out data port bool; end CombinedPatternExample; system implementation CombinedPatternExample.impl subcomponents counter_part : system CounterThresholdExample.impl; consistency_part : system PairwiseConsistencyExample.impl; connections c1 : port reset -> counter_part.reset_counter; c2 : port step -> counter_part.increment_counter; c3 : port value_a -> consistency_part.primary_value; c4 : port value_b -> consistency_part.secondary_value; c5 : port consistency_part.difference_ok -> status; end CombinedPatternExample.impl; end agree_kexp_combined_pattern;

topic: type scope range assumption and guarantee
body: For component type contracts, place input envelope assumptions and output range guarantees inside annex agree only when the case supplies concrete bounds, named constants, or a visible relation. Use case-provided thresholds and legal visible feature names.
For output dependency contracts, write a guarantee that relates visible outputs to visible inputs. Do not use implementation-only subcomponent paths in a component type annex.
For implementation contracts, use assign only when the left-hand side is an existing output feature or declared auxiliary variable. Do not place guarantee statements in implementation scope.
For pre() expressions, declare an initialized state such as initialized : bool = false -> true and guard previous-value comparisons on initialized.
For recursive variables, define an initialized eq expression with -> and pre(x), then relate visible outputs to that state with a separate guarantee or assign.
Subprogram features may be in/out parameters rather than ports. Treat visible parameters like legal AGREE identifiers in the owning subprogram scope.

Rule: AGREE expressions may only reference identifiers visible in the current component scope. Must: use exact current-case names from the model index. Forbid: copying identifiers from examples or inventing ports/components.

Rule: return only the requested structured format. Must: preserve annex agree {** ... **}; delimiters when an annex is requested. Forbid: Markdown fences inside AADL artifacts, free-form explanations, duplicate declarations, and standalone assignments outside legal AGREE constructs.

Rule: component types and implementations have different legal scopes. Must: place assume/guarantee/eq/const in the component type when they describe interface behavior, and implementation-oriented assign/assert clauses in the matching implementation. Forbid: redesigning architecture during fusion/repair.

Guidance: requirements often mention validity, legal operating states, safe boundaries, or algorithm envelopes without giving the actual state set, bound, or relation. Treat those phrases as missing information unless the current requirement or model provides a concrete value, named constant, enumeration state, or visible relation. Use range examples only when the case supplies the bounds or relation to instantiate.
Declare every internal AGREE variable explicitly with eq and a type before use.
Do not redeclare AADL feature names as AGREE eq variables; ports are already visible in legal scopes.
Define int, real, and bool aliases at package level when the model uses those aliases.
Add matching with clauses for package-qualified references such as Base_Types::Float.
Place eq, const, assume, and guarantee clauses in component type annexes for interface behavior.
Place implementation-oriented assign clauses in component implementation annexes.
The left-hand side of assign must already exist as an output feature or declared auxiliary variable.
Do not define the same variable with both an initialized eq expression and an implementation assign.
Use AGREE logical operators and, or, and not (...); do not use &&, ||, or !.
Use = rather than := in AGREE expressions.
Comparison expressions return bool and must not be assigned to numeric variables.
Declare fixed thresholds with const.
Define pre() recurrences with the -> operator in a type-level eq declaration.
Use pre(x) with parentheses.
Use unique quoted labels for labeled assume, guarantee, assert, and assign clauses.
Avoid non-ASCII mathematical or logical symbols in generated artifacts.
Do not call unsupported math-library functions unless they are explicitly provided by a referenced node or package.
Preserve trigger, constraint, and required response in generated contracts.
Use one-way implication => unless the requirement explicitly states equivalence.
Ground every AGREE variable in the current AADL model or an explicit declaration.
Do not reference implementation-only subcomponent paths from incompatible component type scopes.
Treat each annex agree block as scoped to its owning component declaration.
Use implementation-level assignments to bind subcomponent outputs when needed.
Use nested if ... then ... else expressions for branching logic.
Do not use unsupported elsif syntax.

If AGREE reports "Couldn't resolve reference to 'integer'" or "Couldn't resolve reference to 'boolean'" in a const or eq declaration, the generated AGREE type name is invalid. AGREE scalar declaration types are int, real, and bool. Recommended pattern: const lower_limit : int = 0; eq ok : bool = x >= lower_limit;

If AGREE reports "named thing must be an expression with a type" or a guarantee expression has type <error>, trace the first unresolved identifier or invalid helper declaration on the same line. Fix the root unresolved reference, or delete the invalid clause instead of adding architecture. Recommended pattern: Use only visible AADL features or eq helpers declared in the same annex; otherwise remove the guarantee.

If AGREE reports "Couldn't resolve reference to" a port, data type, package, or ModelUnit, do not invent a declaration in repair. Use exact visible identifiers from the current component scope; for package/data type failures, this is usually a model dependency staging issue rather than a contract repair issue. Recommended pattern: Delete or rewrite the AGREE clause to use existing visible identifiers; keep architecture unchanged.

If AGREE reports "The assumed type ... is ... but the actual type is ...", align the helper declaration type with the expression. Comparison expressions are bool; integer literals and integer arithmetic are int; real literals and real arithmetic are real. Recommended pattern: eq range_value : bool = x >= min_value and x <= max_value;

If diagnostics point to implementation-level references or subcomponent paths in a component type annex, move only valid implementation bindings to the implementation annex or delete the invalid guarantee. Component type contracts may reference only features visible at that type scope. Recommended pattern: Use a type-level guarantee over visible ports, or an implementation-level assign when the left-hand side is a valid output.

If diagnostics involve an event port in a numeric or Boolean comparison, delete the clause unless the model provides an explicit data value for the event. Plain AADL event ports are not AGREE numeric values and should not be encoded as 0, 1, true, or false. Recommended pattern: Omit the event-port activation clause or use a model-provided data/event-data value if one exists in the current scope.

If diagnostics point to range comparisons or 0/1 equality over Boolean, enumeration-like, or opaque data ports, remove the generated clause unless the requirement and AADL data representation provide a numeric scalar. Do not convert Boolean domain values into integers. Recommended pattern: Use exact Boolean expressions only when the port is an AGREE bool in scope; otherwise omit the unsafe clause.

If the requirement does not explicitly state non-negative, positive, minimum, maximum, or a numeric interval, do not create a generic x >= 0 assumption for a port just because it looks numeric. Delete invented bounds during repair. Recommended pattern: Keep only bounds directly stated by the requirement and compatible with a numeric AGREE type.

topic: AADL Property Names Are Not AGREE Variables
body: If diagnostics report unresolved references to Compute_Execution_Time, Deadline, Period, Priority, Dispatch_Protocol, Stack_Size, Code_Size, or unit tokens such as ms/us/Hz/Bytes inside an AGREE annex, delete the generated clause. AADL property associations are not automatically in AGREE expression scope as variables. Recommended pattern: Do not encode AADL timing properties as AGREE expressions unless the model exposes explicit typed ports or constants for them.
